rationale: C18 is the strongest plausible template because it establishes investigative access to agency papers, records, and documents in support of Executive Branch investigations into improper governmental conduct. The child compresses that machinery into a targeted direction to one administrator to seize specified housing records for ongoing Executive Branch investigations and related corrective action. C16 and C05 contain record-transfer provisions, but those concern administrative succession rather than investigative custody.

shared_material.child_excerpt: In order to facilitate the investigations which are being conducted by the Executive Branch of the Government and any other actions necessary or proper to insure the fidelity of operations
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Conduct investigations leading to the detection of, and appropriate action with respect to... improper or illegal conduct relating to the performance of official business of the Federal Government.
shared_material.explanation: Both link Executive Branch investigations of governmental misconduct to ensuing corrective or legal action.

shared_material.child_excerpt: you are hereby authorized and directed to take custody forthwith of all files and records
shared_material.parent_excerpt: All executive departments and agencies are authorized and directed to cooperate fully... [and] furnish him... papers, records, and documents, as he may require in the performance of his functions
shared_material.explanation: Both use a presidential direction to secure government records needed for an investigation, with the child adapting general compelled access into immediate custody of a specified record set.
